channel.title: Regula — EU AI Act Regulatory Delta Log
channel.description: Primary-source-linked changelog for the EU AI Act. Every entry is article-keyed and machine-readable.

item.title: [regulation-adoption] Art. 30: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Annex XIV (list of codes, categories and correspondin
item.description: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 inserts Annex XIV into Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, a three-category code list used to scope the designation of notified bodies: AIP codes (product legislation), AIB codes (biometric Annex III systems) and AIH codes (horizontal, technology-specific). Annex XIV Section 3 defines AIH 0401 as "AI systems based on other emerging AI technologies not covered by other codes, including Agentic AI", and AIH 0205 as "AI systems that learn from their environment, excluding AI systems covered under AIH 0401". This is the first appearance of the term Agentic AI in binding Union law, and it appears exactly once in the whole regulation, in that table. It is a nomenclature code for assessor competence, NOT a definition: no article defines an agent, no risk tier is keyed to autonomy, and no obligation attaches to the code. Recital 43 states the code list exists so that notified bodies "are fully competent in regard to the AI systems they are required to assess". (confidence: verified-primary)

item.title: [regulation-adoption] Art. 5, Art. 6, Art. 11, Art. 50, Art. 113: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 8 Jul
item.description: The Digital Omnibus on AI was published in the Official Journal of the European Union on 24 July 2026 as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the AI Act) together with Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 (civil aviation) and Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (machinery). It enters into force on 27 July 2026, the third day following publication. From that date the deferred deadlines are enacted law: Annex III standalone high-risk obligations apply from 2 December 2027, Annex I product-embedded high-risk obligations from 2 August 2028, Article 50(2) watermarking for existing systems from 2 December 2026, and the new Article 5 prohibition on AI-generated CSAM and non-consensual intimate imagery from 2 December 2026. Article 50 transparency duties for new systems keep their 2 August 2026 date, unchanged. (confidence: verified-primary)

item.title: [harmonised-standard] Art. 17, Art. 40: EN 18286:2026, Artificial Intelligence: Quality management system for EU AI Act
item.description: CEN-CENELEC approved EN 18286 on 12 July 2026 and it is published as EN 18286:2026. It is the first AI Act standard from JTC 21 to reach publication, and it operationalises the Article 17 quality management system duty for providers of high-risk AI systems. Its public enquiry ran 30 October 2025 to 22 January 2026. CRITICAL DISTINCTION: publication is not Official Journal citation. As at this entry's verification date the standard has NOT been cited in the OJ, so it does NOT yet confer the Article 40 presumption of conformity, and a provider relying on it carries the full evidentiary burden. Any statement that EN 18286 is unpublished or at formal vote is now false; any statement that it grants presumption of conformity is also false. (confidence: verified-secondary)

item.title: [council-position] Art. 6, Art. 50, Art. 51, Art. 57, Art. 113: Artificial intelligence: Council gives final green light to simplify and streaml
item.description: The Council of the EU gave its final approval to the Digital Omnibus on AI on 29 June 2026, completing the co-legislators' formal adoption after the European Parliament's 16 June plenary vote. This locks in the deferral of Annex III standalone high-risk obligations from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027, and Annex I product-embedded high-risk obligations to 2 August 2028, together with the new prohibitions and the Article 50(2) transition to 2 December 2026. The only remaining step is publication in the Official Journal of the European Union; the act enters into force on the third day after publication. (confidence: verified-primary)

item.title: [parliament-position] Art. 6, Art. 50, Art. 51, Art. 57, Art. 113: AI Act: EP approves simplification measures and "nudifier" app ban
item.description: The European Parliament's plenary approved the Digital Omnibus on AI on 16 June 2026 by 423 votes to 57, with 174 abstentions, endorsing the 7 May provisional agreement. This confirms Parliament's side of the deferral of Annex III high-risk obligations to 2 December 2027 and Annex I product-embedded obligations to 2 August 2028, and the new prohibition on non-consensual intimate deepfakes. The IMCO and LIBE committees had approved the agreed text on 2 June 2026. Formal adoption still required the Council's final approval. (confidence: verified-primary)

item.title: [trilogue-outcome] Art. 6, Art. 50, Art. 51, Art. 57, Art. 113: Artificial intelligence: Council and Parliament agree to simplify and streamline
item.description: The follow-up political trilogue on the Digital Omnibus on AI succeeded on 7 May 2026, reaching a provisional agreement between the Council and the European Parliament after the 28-29 April round had ended without agreement. The agreement defers the application of obligations for standalone high-risk AI systems under Annex III from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027, and for high-risk AI embedded in regulated products under Annex I to 2 August 2028. It also introduces new prohibitions (non-consensual intimate deepfakes / CSAM) applying from 2 December 2026 and moves the Article 50(2) synthetic-content marking transition to 2 December 2026. The provisional agreement was approved by Member States' ambassadors (Coreper) on 13 May 2026. (confidence: verified-primary)

item.title: [amendment-proposal] Art. 6, Art. 13, Art. 26, Art. 43, Art. 50, Art. 113: AI Act Omnibus: first political trilogue ends without agreement
item.description: The first political trilogue on the Digital Omnibus on AI ended without agreement on 29 April 2026 after about 12 hours of negotiations. The sticking point was the conformity-assessment architecture for AI in regulated products under Annex I: Parliament pushed to move sectoral legislation (machinery, medical devices, toys) from Section A to Section B, letting sectoral safety law handle those AI systems; the Council resisted, to preserve AI Act oversight for sensitive sectors. A follow-up trilogue is scheduled for about 13 May 2026. The Cypriot Council Presidency must close the file before its term ends 30 June 2026; otherwise the Lithuanian Presidency takes over from 1 July. If the Omnibus is not formally adopted before 2 August 2026, the original AI Act obligations (Regulation 2024/1689, Article 113) apply as written on that date. Multiple advisory firms (IAPP, DLA Piper, Modulos) now recommend preparing against the original 2 August 2026 deadline rather than the proposed extensions. (confidence: verified-primary)

item.title: [amendment-proposal] Art. 6, Art. 13, Art. 26, Art. 43, Art. 50, Art. 113: Trilogue negotiations — Digital Omnibus on AI (target date)
item.description: Target date for the first trilogue meeting between Council, Parliament and Commission on the Digital Omnibus on AI. Not an adopted change — this entry tracks the calendar milestone so the Regula countdown and the FAQ copy can reflect the live state of negotiations. Once the trilogue outcome is known, this entry will be superseded by a `trilogue-outcome` entry with the specific compromise text. (confidence: reported-unverified)

item.title: [parliament-position] Art. 6, Art. 13, Art. 26, Art. 43, Art. 50, Art. 113: European Parliament — position on the Digital Omnibus on AI (first reading)
item.description: The European Parliament adopts its first-reading position on the Digital Omnibus on AI. The vote establishes Parliament's negotiating mandate for trilogue. Parliament's position broadly supports the deferral but introduces amendments strengthening transparency requirements (Article 50) and narrowing the Article 6(3) narrow-procedural-task carve-out. (confidence: reported-unverified)

item.title: [council-position] Art. 6, Art. 13, Art. 26, Art. 43, Art. 50, Art. 113: Council of the EU — general approach on the Digital Omnibus on AI
item.description: The Council of the European Union adopts its general approach on the Digital Omnibus on AI. Member State representatives agree on a negotiating position that broadly endorses the Commission proposal's deferral of high-risk AI system obligations, with targeted amendments on the scope of Article 6(3) and on Member State sandbox establishment timelines. The general approach opens the door to trilogue negotiations with the European Parliament. (confidence: reported-unverified)

item.title: [amendment-proposal] Art. 6, Art. 13, Art. 26, Art. 43, Art. 50, Art. 113: Digital Omnibus on AI — European Commission proposal for targeted amendments to
item.description: The European Commission publishes the Digital Omnibus on AI: a targeted simplification package proposing to defer the application dates for high-risk AI system obligations and to clarify transparency duties. The proposal shifts the Annex III high-risk deadline from 2 August 2026 to a later date (widely reported as 2 December 2027 in the proposal text), with further deferrals for systems placed on the market before the new application date. Procedural simplifications are proposed for SMEs and for conformity assessment steps. (confidence: verified-primary)

item.title: [regulation-adoption] all articles: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 Ju
item.description: The EU AI Act is published in the Official Journal of the European Union. Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 enters into force 20 days later (1 August 2024). Subsequent application dates are staggered: Article 5 prohibitions from 2 February 2025, General-Purpose AI rules from 2 August 2025, governance and penalty provisions from 2 August 2025, high-risk system obligations from 2 August 2026, and high-risk systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 from 2 August 2027 (per Article 113). (confidence: verified-primary)
